news.title: Cars have become unaffordable for many Americans. Here’s what the numbers show.
news.description: At today’s prices and rates, even the average used vehicle can exceed some commonly used affordability measures.
news.author: Venessa Wong

copy.hook: A $25,000 used car now fails the 10% rule. What changed?
copy.explain: Used-car loans cost about 11% a year, so monthly payments jump. The 10% rule caps car costs at a tenth of income, and many Cars.com shoppers now blow past it.
copy.takeaway: When customers can't afford the product, the middleman feels it too.
copy.question: Would you take a $25,000 used car at 11% interest, or wait for rates to drop?
